title: Add Helm hook jobs for schema migration gating + post-upgrade smoke tests
author: Ines Carvalho
body:
## Context
Private upgrades need deterministic ordering around DB/schema migrations and a fast signal that the post-upgrade control plane/runtime are healthy. Today we rely on “best effort” init containers + operator sequencing, but `helm upgrade` can still roll Deployments before migrations complete (and we don’t get a single gating point that fails the upgrade).

This PR introduces two hook-based Jobs in the chart:
1) **Schema migration gating job** that runs as a Helm **pre-upgrade/pre-install hook** and must succeed before the rest of the release is applied.
2) **Post-upgrade smoke test job** that runs as a Helm **post-upgrade hook** to validate basic APIs and surface failures quickly.

Also adds documentation for ordering guarantees and operational knobs.

## What changed (high level)
- New template: `templates/hooks/schema-migrate-job.yaml`
  - Helm hook: `pre-install,pre-upgrade`
  - Hook weight: `-10` (runs before other hooks; see ordering notes below)
  - Fails the Helm operation if migrations fail or timeout.
  - Optional: can be disabled for break-glass / legacy installs.
- New template: `templates/hooks/post-upgrade-smoke-test-job.yaml`
  - Helm hook: `post-upgrade`
  - Hook weight: `10`
  - Runs lightweight checks against control plane + gateway endpoints.
- Values:
  - `upgrade.migrations.enabled` (default: true)
  - `upgrade.migrations.timeoutSeconds` (default: 1800)
  - `upgrade.smokeTest.enabled` (default: true)
  - `upgrade.smokeTest.timeoutSeconds` (default: 600)
  - `upgrade.smokeTest.mode` (default: "basic"; supports "basic" and "extended")
- Docs:
  - `docs/private-upgrades.md` updated with ordering and troubleshooting
  - Chart README updated with new values and expected behavior

## Ordering guarantees
Helm hook ordering is defined by:
- Hook type ordering (pre-* hooks run before resources are updated; post-* hooks run after)
- Hook weights (lower runs earlier)

This PR guarantees:
- The schema migration Job runs **before** Deployments/StatefulSets for control-plane/runtime components are updated.
- If the migration Job fails, **the Helm upgrade fails** and no updated workloads should be rolled out by Helm.
- The smoke test Job runs **after** Helm has applied updated manifests, and failures are visible as a failed hook (and `helm status` shows it).

Non-goals / limitations (documented):
- Helm hooks do not fully prevent external controllers from restarting workloads (e.g., PDB/evictions) during an upgrade.
- Helm itself won’t roll back automatically on a failed hook unless the caller uses `--atomic` (installer will set this; tracked in ENG-2314).

## Implementation notes
### Schema migration job
- Uses the chart’s existing migration image/entrypoint (no new binary).
- Runs with the same serviceAccount as the control plane (configurable via values) to access DB creds.
- Uses `hook-delete-policy: before-hook-creation,hook-succeeded` to avoid accumulating succeeded jobs while keeping failed jobs for debugging.

Illustrative snippet:
`metadata.annotations`:
- `helm.sh/hook: pre-install,pre-upgrade`
- `helm.sh/hook-weight: "-10"`
- `helm.sh/hook-delete-policy: before-hook-creation,hook-succeeded`

### Post-upgrade smoke test job
- Performs:
  - control plane `/healthz` and `/readyz`
  - version endpoint check (ensures we can read the new component versions)
  - gateway route sanity (HTTP 200 and expected headers)
- Emits structured JSON to stdout for Support ingestion (installer can capture logs into diagnostics bundle).

## Backwards compatibility
- Default behavior is safe for existing installs: migration gating and smoke tests are enabled by default, but can be disabled if a customer environment is mid-transition.
- No required value changes for existing releases; new values are additive.

## How to test
- `helm template` / `helm lint` passes.
- Manual:
  - Install chart, then simulate an upgrade with a migration that intentionally fails -> Helm upgrade fails at pre-upgrade hook.
  - Upgrade with a healthy migration -> deployments roll, then post-upgrade smoke test runs and succeeds.

Commands used (kind):
- `helm upgrade --install redwood ./charts/redwood-private -n redwood --create-namespace --atomic --timeout 45m`

## Screenshots / output
- `helm status redwood -n redwood` shows `pre-upgrade` and `post-upgrade` hook Jobs with clear names and timestamps.

## Checklist
- [x] Hook jobs respect namespace + labels conventions
- [x] Values documented
- [x] Default timeouts conservative for enterprise DB sizes
- [x] Security review: no secrets in logs; SA/RBAC unchanged by default

---

### Review conversation (highlights)
**Michael Nguyen:** "Can we ensure the migration Job uses the same DB connection settings as the control plane? We’ve had drift when charts duplicated env var wiring."

**Ines Carvalho (author):** "Yep — I refactored to reuse the existing `controlPlane.env` helper template and pass the exact same env var set into the hook job. Added a unit test in `tests/template_test.go` to assert parity for the DB-related vars."

**Sean Gallagher:** "Concern: hook jobs can pile up and clutter namespaces. Also prefer keeping failed jobs for triage."

**Ines Carvalho:** "Configured `hook-delete-policy` to delete on success and before re-creation; failed jobs remain. Added doc note on `kubectl logs job/<name>`."

**Marcus Lin:** "Any chance smoke test prints tokens/headers? We should avoid leaking auth in stdout since installer will scoop logs into diagnostics bundles."

**Ines Carvalho:** "Good call. Updated smoke test script to explicitly redact `Authorization` and to avoid dumping response bodies by default. Docs now say `upgrade.smokeTest.mode=extended` still doesn’t print headers."

**Connor O'Brien:** "Please document the exact ordering guarantee and what it does NOT guarantee (atomic rollback depends on installer flags)."

**Ines Carvalho:** "Added a dedicated ‘Ordering guarantees’ section + mention of `--atomic` requirement. Linked ENG-2314 for installer wiring."
